question: Inferring from passage, what is the most practical way of reducing the health risk of subway life?
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes multiple sources of pollution in the subway system, including train parts and other materials on the tracks.
 
• While no direct solutions are provided in the text, 'Option 1' (Generating ventilation systems) can be inferred as a practical way to reduce air pollution in the subway. Improved ventilation systems can help to circulate fresh air and remove some of the particulate matter.
 
• This method tackles the problem at its core - the polluted air in the subway environment - rather than working around it or avoiding it altogether.
 
• Though it would require investment and infrastructure changes, if implemented correctly, it could benefit all subway users and workers, making it a holistic solution to the problem.

Therefore, the correct answer is - **'Option 1'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• 'Option 2' (Opting for other transportation modes) and 'Option 4' (Reducing subway commutation) are impractical pedestrian-level solutions that don't address the root of the problem. Many people are reliant on subway systems for daily travel and so, avoiding subway use might not be an option.
 
• 'Option 3' (Wearing face masks during journey) could reduce exposure to airborne particles for individuals, but it doesn't diminish the source of pollution which is inherent to the subway environment.
 
• Hence, implementing a better ventilation system would be a more effective strategy to clean the air in the subway systems.
